name: Gibbon
tagline: no engine: it moves only on its webs, like Spider-Man without gravity
summary: The web-slinger (Yash, 2026-10-18: like Spider-Man). No engine at all: the Gibbon sits still until it shoots a web. The sticks turn it to aim; LT shoots the left hand's web and RT the right's at whatever is near the crosshair (a prism of the course, mass, a rival's trail, a crystal). A web flies out, latches, and is an elastic bungee: hold the trigger and it pulls you in, springy and bouncing; latch off to the side and you swing round the anchor, faster as the web shortens. Let go and you fly on your momentum; shoot the next web before you lose it. Hand over hand, never a thruster.

spec.v: only on its webs: no throttle, no thruster
LT left hand · RT right hand · 220 u, latch on anything
elastic bungee: springy pull, swing, spin-up, bounce off walls

fantasy: A brachiator in space. It never flies straight for long: it hooks the world and swings through it, and the mass other pilots lay is its forest canopy.
why: Grapple and swing is the second hottest movement verb of 2024-26 (Spider-Man 2 at 11M+, Marvel Rivals' most-loved heroes are its swingers, Echo Point Nova 98% positive). The forgiveness rules come from Echo Point Nova: a target is remembered for half a second after you looked past it, and the rope lets go on its own when it stops making sense.

charge.tip: A proposal: Charge is the web's spring. A stiffer web yanks harder and bounces quicker.

controls.lt: left web (hold = pull, let go = fly)
controls.rt: right web (hold = pull, let go = fly)
rows: the sticks only turn the Gibbon (it has no engine) · aim near something and squeeze: the web flies out, latches and pulls · hold to keep pulling, let go to fly on · the rings show what each hand would hit
latch off to one side of where you are going and you swing round the anchor, faster as the web shortens · two webs pull against each other · a wall you hit bounces you
controls.gamepad: sticks turn the Gibbon to aim (it has no engine and no throttle) · LT left web · RT right web (hold = pull, let go = fly)
controls.keys: W S pitch · A D yaw · Q E roll (aim) · Space left web · F right web (hold = pull, let go = fly)

notModelled: There is no gravity: a 'swing' is the elastic web's central pull, not a pendulum. Real Spider-Man swings fall into the bottom of the arc; this one orbits the anchor.
Space drag (0.12 per s, lab-only) lets a coasting Gibbon come to rest; true space would be 0.
The aim helps you the way the Spider-Man games do: a web latches on the best thing inside a 22-degree cone round the crosshair, preferring far anchors, each hand preferring its own side.

Webs latch on prisms of every kind (the course ribbon included) and on crystals; they never cut, own or move what they hold. The Unity Tether prototype on cece/loving-feynman-hlgf18 is a different design (auto-tethers, a rigid long tether) kept for reference.
The web is drawn as a twisted two-strand line, after the flora's spindles; the game would need its own web visual.
sources: Design: Yash 2026-10-18 ('like Spider-Man, no auto moving, it moves only when it shoots a web, elastic and springy'); Docs/Studios/CONCEPT_FLEET.md section 8.3. The previous round-2 version (two modes on the Tether prototype) is section 8.2 and the `tether` kind.
